question.:question/problem: Which of the following is a lower triangular matrix?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that $E$ is a matrix for which all entries *above* the diagonal are $0$'s:

$$
E=\begin{bmatrix}7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{bmatrix}
$$

Hence, it is a lower triangular matrix. 

By contrast, matrices $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$ each have at least one non-zero entry above the diagonal:

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}7 & -8 \\ 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
B=\begin{bmatrix}-7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 7 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
C=\begin{bmatrix}-10 & 0 & -10 \\ 0 & -7 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -7\end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
D=\begin{bmatrix}3 & -9 \\ 0 & -8\end{bmatrix}
$$

So, they are not lower triangular matrices.
